questions.question: Objects that are symmetric can be shown effectively using this type of section -
questions.solution:
__Explanation:__

Section:

__
 
• Sectional views are drawn to show the internal details of an object.
 
• The object is assumed to be cut on a plane.
 
• The surface produced by cutting an object at this plane is called a section.
 
• The surface which cuts the object at the section plane is shown hatched (a regular pattern) according to standard conventions.
 
• Sections are of many types:
 
 
• Full section
 
• Offset section
 
• Half section
 
• Revolved section
 
• Removed section
 
• Partial section, or broken section
 
• Auxillary section
 
• Aligned section. 
 
 
 
• The type of section to be adopted depends upon the shape of the object.

Half section:

 
• This is generally used for symmetrical objects.
 
• Two cutting planes at right angles to each other pass halfway through the view up to the centerline.
 
• Thus only one quarter is assumed to be removed.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/97bed8abf75b7e7e9b456e25c70482f53b57b5186aa73959e6d49bfe3b6800c2.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Revolved section:

 
• It is used to show the cross-section shape of ribs, arms, spoke, etc. The section line is drawn by passing a cutting plane at right angles to the axis.
 
• This section is then revolved and drawn at the cutting plane axis on the main view. If the cross-section changes along the length, many revolved sections can be drawn. 
 
• ​​When the sectional view is shown within the object it is known as a Revolved section.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/105facc8d3edab5af6fc958c4f1c61c5ee2f4444ef847aba14f9d87393971895.png] 

​

Removed section:

 
• It is similar to Revolved section, but instead of drawing the section on the view, it is drawn in a free space near the object along the centerline of the section.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2eb07337aead819d6cbef20a6b55e0c128ddac32de484a5ae7c10e3aa189785d.png] 

 

Partial section:

 
• A section consisting of less than half a section is called a partial section. Note that here we use a broken line to indicate the division between the sectioned and unsectioned part. For this reason, a partial section is often called a Broken section.

​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/457281b4dd25fe5d42cf8eca6eb23a38e4e00ddc3a81e6e7ee1cee6f383db9ff.png] 

Aligned section:

 
• An aligned section view/cut is a view created from a cutting profile defined from non-parallel planes. In order to include in a section a certain angled element, the cutting plane may be bent so as to pass through those features. The plane and feature are then imagined to be revolved into the original plane.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8b8bc818d8eeaeef5e73e0f0fbc4dab1c7b2c16fa3dd1bcf43edba45f7a3e9bc.png] 

Full section:

 
• The cutting plane passes entirely through the object in a straight line. Thin objects like ribs, etc. are not hatched even if they are cut by the cutting plane along the axis.
 
• To see the internal features of an object that are not in a straight line, the cutting plane can be offset. Such a section is called the Offset section. The cutting plane can be inclined also.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/10fb3e9e7196724ce81d02410bff9ee4eeb98df72f48b731b1340c026f834cbe.png] 

57:T2d

options.text: If three forces acting on a body are said to be in equilibrium, then each force is directly dependent on sine of the angle between the other two forces.
If three forces are non-coplanar, then each force is directly dependent on sine of the angle between the other two forces.
If three forces are not in equilibrium, then each force is inversely proportional to sine of the angle between the other two forces.
If two forces are in equilibrium, then each force is directly proportional to sine of the angle between them.

questions.solution:

Consider three forces F1, F2, F3 acting on a particle or rigid body making angles α, β, and γ with each other.

questions.question: Once in how many years the refilling should done in water type fire extinguisher?
questions.solution:
**Concept**

 
• Fire extinguishers are active fire protection devices that require regular maintenance to ensure reliability during an emergency.
 
• Maintenance procedures include periodic inspection, refilling (recharging), and hydrostatic pressure testing.
 
• The frequency of refilling is determined by the type of extinguishing agent and the specific safety standards (such as IS 2190 or NFPA guidelines).

**
**Explanation**

Fire extinguishers must be serviced and refilled at specific intervals to ensure the extinguishing agent is effective and the expellant gas pressure is maintained.

For a Water Type Fire Extinguisher**:

 
• **Refilling:** According to standard safety regulations and maintenance schedules for fire fighting equipment, water-type extinguishers (both gas cartridge and stored pressure types) should be refilled once every **2 years**.
 
• **Hydraulic Testing:** Apart from refilling, the extinguisher shell must undergo a hydraulic pressure test every 3 years to ensure the cylinder can withstand the operating pressure.
 
• **Routine Check:** They should also be inspected quarterly or half-yearly for any physical damage, nozzle blockage, or pressure loss.

Regular refilling prevents the accumulation of sediment or biological growth in the water and ensures that the mechanical parts of the discharge mechanism remain functional.

**Hence, the refilling of a water type fire extinguisher should be done once in every 2 years.**

questions.question: The thickness of a thread is measured by a student using a microscope of magnification 100. After making 30 observations, he finds the average width of the thread is 5.7 mm. What is the estimated thickness of the thread?
questions.solution:
__**Concept:**__

When a measurement is taken using a microscope, the **actual thickness** of an object is obtained by dividing the observed (magnified) width by the magnification.

__**Given:**__

__
 
• Magnification of microscope = 100
 
• Average observed width = 5.7 mm

**Calculation:**__

 {Actual thickness} = dfrac{{Observed width}}{{Magnification}} = dfrac{5.7}{100} 

 {Actual thickness} = 0.057 {mm}

questions.question: The angular velocity (in radians /sec) of a body rotating at N rpm is:
questions.solution:
Rpm is just a measure of how many times a point is revolving per minute.

In a single revolution, a point rotates an angle = 2π

So, the total angle a point is rotating per minute = N x 2 π

The angular velocity is a measure of how fast it is rotating = Angle Rotated/Time Required = **2π N/60**

questions.question:
A body of weight 100 N is lying on a rough horizontal surface, and the horizontal force of 50 N is applied on the body as shown in the figure, which is just enough to move the body. What will be the coefficient of friction? 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ff400d0417184de8750b9f91c10feba21fa0a4d204ef7dbbc2f45b25a3b57134.png]
questions.solution:
__Concept-__

Friction-

 
• Sliding friction can be defined as the resistance created by any two objects when sliding against each other.
 
• This friction is also known as kinetic friction and is defined as the force that is needed to keep a surface sliding along another surface.
 
• It depends on two variables- one is material and the other is the weight of the object. Any change in the surface area in contact does not change the sliding friction. 
 
• 
 
The equation for sliding force includes the coefficient of sliding friction times the normal force.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ff400d0417184de8750b9f91c10feba21fa0a4d204ef7dbbc2f45b25a3b57134.png] ​

Fs = μFn 

Where FS = force of sliding friction,Fn = normal force , μ = Coefficient of sliding friction

Given data and calculation-

Body weight = Fn = 100 N

Friction force = 50 N

Coefficient of friction = (50)/(100) = 0.5

questions.question: “A” in the ABC of first aid stands for ____.
questions.solution:
__Explanation:__

First aid 

 
• First aid is defined as the immediate care and support given to an acutely injured or ill person, primarily to save life, 
 
• First aid procedure often consists of simple and basic life-saving techniques that an individual performs with proper training and knowledge. 

The key aims of first aid can be summarized in three key points 

 
• Preserve life: If the patient was breathing, a first aider would normally place them in the recovery position, with the patient leant over on their side, which also has the effect of clearing the tongue from the pharynx. The first aider will be taught to deal with this through a combination of 'back slaps' and 'abdominal thrusts'. Once the airway has been opened, the first aider would assess to see if the patient is breathing. 
 
• Prevent further harm: Also sometimes called prevent 
 
• the condition from worsening, or danger of further injury, this covers both external factors, such as moving a patient away from any cause of harm, and applying first aid techniques to prevent worsening of the condition, such as applying pressure to stop a bleed becoming dangerous. 
 
• Promote recovery: First aid also involves trying to start the recovery process from the illness or injury, and in some cases might involve completing a treatment, such as in the case of applying a plaster to a small wound. 

 

ABC of first aid:

 
• **ABC stands for airway, breathing and circulation. **

 
 
• Airway: Attention must first be brought to the airway to ensure it is clear. Obstruction (choking) is a life-threatening emergency. 
 
• Breathing: If breathing stops, the victim may die soon. Hence means of providing support for breathing is an important next step. There are several methods practiced in first aid. 
 
• Circulation: Blood circulation is vital to keep a person alive. The first aiders are now trained to go straight to chest compressions through CPR methods

questions.question:
Identify the orthographic symbol of a pipe fitting shown in the figure.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5905e33f18e471327d05b5feb8e1b07d9ea6f71436c0ac13fbd0b365fe31979f.png]
questions.solution:
__**Explanation:**__

**Orthographic Symbol of Pipe Fitting**

**Definition:** An orthographic symbol is a simplified representation or a graphical depiction used in engineering drawings to represent a component, such as a pipe fitting. These symbols are standardized to convey the type and function of the component without the need for detailed pictorial drawings.

**Pipe Fittings:** Pipe fittings are components used in piping systems to connect straight sections of pipe, adapt to different sizes or shapes, and regulate or measure the flow of fluids. Common types of pipe fittings include tees, crosses, unions, bends, elbows, and reducers. Each type has its unique orthographic symbol for representation in engineering drawings.

**Correct Option Analysis:**

The correct option is:

**Option 2:** Cross

The orthographic symbol shown in the figure represents a **cross fitting**. A cross fitting is used to connect four pipe sections at a single point. It has one inlet and three outlets (or vice versa) arranged at 90-degree angles to one another, forming a cross-like structure. In orthographic projections, the symbol for a cross fitting is typically depicted as a cross (+) to indicate the intersecting connection points.

**Key Features of a Cross Fitting:**

__
 
• Used in piping systems where four pipes meet at a single junction.
 
• Commonly employed in systems requiring even distribution of fluids or gases to multiple directions.
 
• Can handle high-pressure and high-temperature applications depending on the material.

**Applications:**

 
• Plumbing and water distribution systems.
 
• Oil and gas pipelines where multiple branches are required.
 
• HVAC systems for air distribution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

To further understand the analysis, let’s evaluate the other options:

**Option 1:** Tee

A tee fitting is used to connect three pipe sections at a single point, forming a T-shaped configuration. It has one inlet and two outlets (or vice versa) arranged at 90-degree angles to one another. The orthographic symbol for a tee fitting typically resembles the letter "T". However, the given figure does not match this description, as the symbol clearly represents four connection points, not three.

**Option 3:** Union

A union fitting is used to connect two pipes while allowing for easy disconnection and reconnection. It is commonly used in systems requiring frequent maintenance or inspection. The orthographic symbol for a union is typically a pair of concentric circles or a symbol indicating a detachable connection. The given figure does not represent a union fitting, as it shows intersecting connections rather than a detachable joint.

**Option 4:** Bend

A bend fitting is used to change the direction of flow in a piping system, typically at an angle such as 90 degrees or 45 degrees. The orthographic symbol for a bend is usually a curved line or an arc representing the change in direction. The given figure does not depict a curved or directional change, ruling out this option.
